exposure: air temperature exposure (extreme high temperature, moderate high temperature)
cohort: A total of 117,515 pregnant women (3,314 with PE and 114,201 with normal pregnancies) were recruited in early pregnancy and followed until delivery in Guangzhou, China.
finding: Exposure to extreme and moderate high ambient temperature during early pregnancy (weeks 1-8) was associated with an increased risk of preeclampsia, with a higher risk observed in women with higher pre-pregnancy BMI.
